# Ein Sof Captions — Phase One: Unbounded Revelation

The Awtsmoos hides infinite visual possibility inside one quiet point of light;
Awtsmoos.com should let the user summon complexity only when the moment is right.

## What the existing engine really is

The 893-line root Captions document is not a simple caption form. It is a local 1080×1920 generative visual compositor with: batch captions; optional headers; box color/opacity/padding/radius; Hebrew particle fields; fragmented/full glyph modes; three connection algorithms; base background color; film grain; bloom; per-property randomization ranges; IndexedDB persistence; optional File System Access directory output; Web Worker rendering; layered nebula/star backgrounds; bloom maps; text fitting; chromatic aberration; vignette/grain; and JPEG downloads.

The problem is not missing capability. The problem is revelation order: every capability is visible at once, the 500px control wall competes with a fixed 540×960 preview, advanced controls are always expanded, randomization toggles are unlabeled decorative glyph spans, the generate button pulses forever, status flickers forever, and several renderer helpers are compressed into unreadable one-line functions.

## Ideal interaction universe

- Preview dominates the screen; controls become a retractable studio rail.
- On desktop the rail is resizable-looking but fixed in purpose, with a single collapse control.
- On mobile the rail becomes a full-height off-canvas drawer; preview remains usable behind it.
- “Essentials” stays open: caption batch, header, generate, save destination.
- “Caption Vessel” is a retractable group for box appearance.
- “Particle Field” retracts density/size/style/characters.
- “Connections” retracts network type/density.
- “Atmosphere” retracts background/grain/bloom.
- Every randomized property has a small real button labeled Randomize; activating it reveals min/max controls only for that property.
- Generation feedback is a calm progress rail/status chip, not an infinite flicker.
- A generation button can have one restrained sheen on hover/focus, never continuous motion.
- Preview uses a bounded aspect-ratio vessel with actual canvas scaling, never a fixed viewport-breaking box.
- Controls use compact two-column rows where safe and one column on narrow screens.
- All forms have visible focus and practical touch targets.
- Reduced-motion disables reveal transforms and canvas-shell micro-motion.
- Batch generation and file-system output remain intact.
- User settings remain persisted under the same IndexedDB database/store/version so existing saved values survive.
- Worker rendering remains off-main-thread.

## Extreme architecture possibilities

A. Keep worker inline and only split UI — rejected because the worker contains minified functions and keeps the monolith hidden inside HTML.
B. Move all worker logic to one 400-line worker file — rejected by the 120-line law.
C. Module Worker with small rendering modules — winner: clean imports, testable pure helpers, no inline blob construction.
D. Move rendering to main thread — rejected because particle/network/postprocessing work can block interaction.
E. Reuse `/captions/video/` renderer — rejected because it is a different product contract and would risk collapsing two distinct tools.

## Phase-one behavioral preservation

- Canvas internal resolution remains 1080×1920.
- Blank caption input still yields one blank vision rather than hard failure.
- Paragraphs split on blank lines for batch output.
- All existing controls/default values remain represented.
- Randomized colors remain random hex colors; numeric ranges honor min/max and range step semantics.
- Worker still emits progress/result/complete messages.
- JPEG quality remains 0.92.
- Directory picker remains optional when supported, with download fallback.
- File naming retains `BH_<timestamp>_EinSof_<sanitized>_<index>.jpg` semantics.
- Existing IndexedDB name/store/version remain `EinSofEngineDB`, `settingsStore`, version 2.
